meta.description: sparc is a Claude Code plugin. It keeps specs, architecture and documents in sync with the code while agents write it.

index.title: sparc: spec-driven work with agents
index.heading: Specs, architecture and code. In sync at each step.

facts.requiresValue: Claude Code or GitHub Copilot CLI, OpenSpec, Node.js, git

index.lede: A plugin for coding agents on OpenSpec. Five roles take each idea to a reviewed and tested change.

steps.name: Review
steps.text: A fresh agent reads the diff.
steps.pain: The agent reviews its own work.

steps.name: Verify
steps.text: Lint, tests and evidence must pass.

documents.heading: Each document has one owner
documents.intro: /sparc:init adds these files. A role is a rule file that a skill follows.

record.heading: sparc is built with sparc
record.intro: Each change to sparc went through this loop.

items.q: Which coding agents does sparc support?
items.a: Claude Code (CLI and Claude Desktop) and GitHub Copilot CLI. The README tells what is not tested with Copilot, for example Copilot in VS Code and the cloud agent: Supported Agents.

items.q: Can I use sparc in an existing code base?
items.a: Yes. Run /sparc:init in the folder of the project. The architect documents what it finds in the code.

items.q: Must a small fix go through the full loop?
items.a: Yes. Each change of behavior goes through propose, apply and archive. This is the cost of specs and documents that stay correct.

items.q: Does sparc work with pull requests?
items.a: Yes. Choose the workflow trunk or pull-request in openspec/config.yaml. In the pull request workflow, the review or the merge is the approval.

2. What this site does not do

This site sets no cookies and stores nothing in your browser. It uses no analytics and no tracking. It loads no content from other servers. The fonts and images come from this site.

3. Hosting and server log

Hetzner Online GmbH, Industriestr. 25, 91710 Gunzenhausen, Germany, hosts this site (privacy policy of Hetzner).

When you open a page, your browser sends technical data. The server keeps this data in its access log:

  • your IP address and port
  • the date and time of the request
  • the requested page, with its address and query, and the result of the request
  • your browser and operating system (user agent)

We use this data only to deliver the site and to keep it safe, for example to find attacks. We do not combine it with other data. The access log has a fixed maximum size. When the log is full, the server deletes the oldest entries. The legal basis is Art. 6 (1) (f) GDPR: our legitimate interest in a safe and available website.

4. Contact by e-mail

If you send us an e-mail, we use your data only to answer you. The legal basis is Art. 6 (1) (b) or (f) GDPR. We delete the data when we do not need it any more and no law tells us to keep it.

5. Links to GitHub

Links to the repository open github.com. The GitHub General Privacy Statement applies there.

6. Your rights

You have the right of access (Art. 15 GDPR), rectification (Art. 16 GDPR), erasure (Art. 17 GDPR), restriction of processing (Art. 18 GDPR), data portability (Art. 20 GDPR) and objection (Art. 21 GDPR). To use these rights, write to kontakt@vensas.de. You can also complain to a supervisory authority, for example the Unabhängiges Datenschutzzentrum Saarland.
